source.title: Bit-Identical Medical Deep Learning via Structured Orthogonal Initialization

record.tranche_reason: Compares structured and Kaiming initialization and reports a validation learning-curve difference, bearing on V4's claim about initialization and learning speed. It does not report training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test AUC and CIFAR-100 test accuracy, but not training classification error, so those results do not establish V1. It also does not test depth limits or shortcut removal. The validation-curve comparison in Figure 3 is the only reported result bearing on a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study uses orthogonal initialization and Fixup-inspired residual scaling to build a deterministic training pipeline. Its validation AUC curves measure held-out predictive performance, without establishing faster optimization, greater trainable depth, or the signal-propagation mechanism named in V4. Its own results do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusions about initialization performance and variability. Their main conclusion is that the complete pipeline produces MD5-verified identical trained weights. They report improved ECG test AUC, no significant mean differences among structured bases or on seven MedMNIST tasks, and CIFAR-100 equivalence. Full determinism through golden batch ordering carries a performance cost. Their interpretation of validation curves as improved optimization stability does not directly establish faster training convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses analytically constructed structured orthogonal initialization, including mixed bases and Fixup residual scaling, and compares it with Kaiming; reports validation AUC rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization method changes the reported validation learning curves; the text says mixed-basis initialization has higher validation AUC and lower variance from epoch 20 onward.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed initialization has higher validation AUC and lower variability from epoch 20 onward in the residual Conformer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured initialization can improve held-out learning trajectories and reduce variability in ECG classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.2.2 reports gradient explosion at residual scaling 1.0 and best test AUC at 0.01. Appendix D analyzes energy preservation and conditioning of idealized DCT linear maps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual branch scaling affects stability in this structured initialization recipe, and idealized DCT maps have favorable norm-preservation properties; neither result establishes V4's plain-network speed or depth effects.

record.problems: The learning-curve comparison is shown in a figure without epoch-specific values in the text. It uses validation AUC rather than training error, and does not establish faster convergence or greater trainable depth directly.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results were extracted: test AUC, per-class variability, and CIFAR-100 accuracy do not measure the training-error behavior or other conditions named in the versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including CIFAR-10/100 with corrupted or random labels, and its dependence on size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation across depth in plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.

Faster optimization and greater trainable depth in plain networks through activation-matched signal and gradient preservation; matched-variance orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh comparisons; and extremely deep plain CNN training.
Recovery or divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, accompanying curvature changes, and sustained edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and equivalent speed and stability using the complete Fixup recipe.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are warranted for the listed versions. The record already declares omission of test AUC, per-class variability, and CIFAR-100 test accuracy; these are not missing measurements of the specified claims.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, including on CIFAR-10/100 and with corrupted or random labels.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and width changes relative to teacher size.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, and the effects of normalization or shortcut removal.

Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation measurements, plain tanh networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights at matched variance, 10,000-layer CNNs, and explicit maximum trainable depth.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss increases and curvature changes, and sharpness at the edge of stability.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual networks without normalization.

rows.subject: Conformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared mixed-basis structured initialization with Kaiming initialization; validation AUC learning curves shown in Figure 3.

conditions.value: Adam, lr=10−3, cosine annealing over 85 epochs

rows.value: Mixed-basis initialization; higher validation AUC with lower variance from epoch 20 onward; precise values figure only
rows.uncertainty: Figure shows mean ±1 std bands; exact values not stated
rows.note: Text describes the curve comparison but supplies no epoch-specific values. The result concerns validation learning curves, not training error or explicit time-to-convergence.
rows.check: Higher validation AUC from epoch 20 onward does not establish faster training convergence or greater trainable depth. The Conformer contains residual connections, and the mixed configuration also includes sqrt class weighting; the comparison does not isolate orthogonality or activation-matched initialization. Structured runs vary batch ordering, whereas Kaiming runs vary initialization seeds. Figure 3 and Sections 4.2 and 5 are the relevant locators.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
